key_insight: Model choice drives AI peer-review error detection most strongly, while verification tools offer gains that depend on the task and scientific domain.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate reviewer models before adding scaffolding, then target citation retrieval, computer algebra, and code execution where they provide measurable value.
method: Inject localisable general, mathematical, numerical, and citation errors at three severity levels into real papers.
Measure detection by error type and severity, plus false positives on clean copies.
Test Skepthical, a multi-agent reviewer using citation retrieval, computer algebra, and executed code.
evidence_signal: Across 30 astrophysics and ML preprints with 357 injected errors, 12 reviewer systems were evaluated; three frontier models given the same prompt differed by about 50 percentage points in total detection on both corpora.
watch_item: Tool gains may not generalise across domains: Skepthical’s citation-detection lead in astrophysics was not statistically distinguishable from the best single LLM in ML.
paper_title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
